photos.caption: Vicky Zhang, center, performs with Taiko SOBA at Palo Alto's Obon Festival in 2025. Taiko is a traditional Japanese percussion art, common at festivals like Obon.
photos.alt: A young woman laughs joyfully while raising taiko drumsticks above her head during an outdoor festival performance, with other drummers visible behind her.

photos.caption: Children dressed in yukata participate in the Bon Odori, a dance performed by the community at the end of the festival.
photos.alt: Two young girls wearing floral yukata and traditional hair accessories stand side by side watching a festival performance, smiling.

photos.caption: Two intergenerational community members share in the Bon Odori. This dance is said to come from the origin of the Obon festival, where Moggallana (one of the Buddha's closest disciples) danced with joy when his mother was freed from the plane of Hungry Ghosts.
photos.alt: An elderly man with white hair and an orange happi coat holds a young boy dressed in a patterned kimono against a bright blue sky.

photos.caption: Alice Smith, executive director of the National Voter Corps, speaks out against the SAVE Act at the Palo Alto 'Good Trouble Lives On' rally.
photos.alt: An elderly white woman in glasses and a white blazer speaks passionately into a microphone at an outdoor rally beneath a 'Good Trouble Lives On' banner.

photos.caption: A young protester holds a sign at the 'Good Trouble Lives On' rally in Palo Alto, honoring the legacy of the late Congressman John Lewis.
photos.alt: A young girl holds a large handwritten sign reading 'Resist — Defend Democracy, Fight Fascism' at an outdoor rally surrounded by other protesters.

photos.caption: Attendees at the 'Good Trouble Lives On' rally in Palo Alto chat while one holds a sign overhead.
photos.alt: A person holds a cardboard sign reading 'It's Up To Us Resist!' alongside an American flag at an outdoor rally under tree cover.

photos.caption: A black-tailed deer pauses on a trail at Edgewood Preserve, where wildlife coexists with one of the most ecologically sensitive habitats on the Peninsula.
photos.alt: A brown deer with large ears looks directly at the camera against a blurred green and golden field background.

photos.caption: Lucy Zhou launches into her relay leg swimming for Palo Alto High School. Zhou now swims for Michigan Institute of Technology.
photos.alt: A swimmer in a black one-piece suit dives off a starting block into a pool lane during a swim meet, body fully extended in the air.

photos.caption: Walmart associates dance together to a mariachi band as community members — including Mayor Ellen Kamei — gather to celebrate the opening of the upgraded Walmart 'Supercenter.'
photos.alt: A group of women wearing blue 'Happy to Help' vests dance in a circle holding hands in a parking lot while a crowd looks on.

about.name: Grace Gormley
about.tagline: Journalism and data science student at Northwestern University Medill
about.bio: I am a journalism and data science double major in my sophomore year at Northwestern University, in the Medill School of Journalism. I strive to combine my data science skills with people-centric reporting to hold those in power accountable and tell important stories. I get excited about investigative and watchdog journalism driven by data.

suso_camp.overview: Stand Up, Speak Out: Journalism for Young Activists is a project Grace undertook for her Girl Scout Gold Award. She wanted to address problems in journalism by combining her passions for teaching, public speaking, service, and journalism. The project took almost an entire year and more than 100 hours of work.
suso_camp.impact: ~70 students, 200+ magazines printed, camp continued in 2024 without Grace's direct involvement

pillars.name: Writing
pillars.description: Over 70 students wrote articles with research and peer quotes about topics they care about, including teen homelessness and climate change.

pillars.name: Public Speaking
pillars.description: Students rehearsed and read their articles aloud to classrooms, building confidence in public speaking.

pillars.name: Results
pillars.description: Student stories were compiled into three printed magazines (one per grade). Nearly $1,000 was fundraised to print over 200 total magazines for students to take home.

pillars.name: Longevity
pillars.description: Grace created a website with all resources needed to replicate the camp. She worked with local organizations to ensure continuation and contacted dozens of journalism teachers to spread SUSO nationwide. The camp continued in 2024 with DreamCatchers without her direct involvement.
